h: notch2 mutations (rossi; kiel) two companion studies: whole-exome sequencing with copy-number analysis (rossi), and whole-genome sequencing with sanger confirmation in 99 cases (kiel) rossi: notch2 was the most frequently mutated gene, in about 20% of cases, with mutations removing the c-terminal pest domain; other notch pathway genes (notch1, spen, dtx1) were also affected, and marginal zone development pathways were deregulated in about 60% of cases. kiel: notch2 mutations in 25 of 99 splenic cases (about 25%) and 1 of 19 non-splenic marginal zone lymphomas, in none of the other b-cell tumors tested, and associated with relapse, transformation or death (p=.002) recurrent somatic mutations genomic studies 2012 splenic marginal zone lymphoma marginal zone lymphomas: gastric malt, non-gastric malt, nodal and splenic

n: Rituximab vs other treatment, two-center series (Else)

d: Chlorambucil 6 mg/m2 daily for 6 weeks then 14 days every 28 days for four cycles, alone or with rituximab 375 mg/m2 (eight doses); after 252 patients a third arm of rituximab alone was added (1:1:6); no previous systemic anticancer therapy

d: Splenectomy as first treatment, 1997-2012

n: Genetics of nodal marginal zone lymphoma (Spina)
d: Whole-exome, targeted and whole-transcriptome sequencing with SNP arrays in 35 patients
h: genetics of nodal marginal zone lymphoma (spina) whole-exome, targeted and whole-transcriptome sequencing with snp arrays in 35 patients 41 genes recurrently affected in at least 3 cases, most often mll2/kmt2d (34%), ptprd (20%), notch2 (20%) and klf2 (17%). ptprd lesions were enriched in nodal disease across mature b-cell tumors, were absent in splenic marginal zone lymphoma, caused loss of phosphatase activity and were associated with cell-cycle deregulation and a higher proliferation index recurrently mutated genes and pathways genomic study 2016 nodal marginal zone lymphoma marginal zone lymphomas: gastric malt, non-gastric malt, nodal and splenic

d: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of marginal zone lymphomas
h: esmo guidelines (zucca) esmo clinical practice guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of marginal zone lymphomas main recommendations (full paper, with its corrigendum): gastric malt lymphoma: h. pylori eradication for all patients, whatever the stage [ii, a]; fish for t(11;18) may identify patients unlikely to respond [iii, b]; watch and wait for persistent stable residual disease [iv, c]. localized malt lymphoma: involved-site radiotherapy is preferred, 24 gy standard (24-30 gy to the stomach), 4 gy possible in the elderly, for palliation or at critical sites; antibiotics may be considered for ocular adnexal disease. systemic options for malt lymphoma: rituximab-chlorambucil [i, a], bendamustine-rituximab [iii, a], rituximab alone [iii, b], lenalidomide-rituximab [iii, c], r-chop for transformation; no published data support rituximab maintenance [iii, d]. splenic: watch and wait if asymptomatic; rituximab alone is the preferred initial therapy [iii, a]; splenectomy in selected cases [iv, b]. nodal: treat on the principles used for follicular lymphoma [iv, b]. hcv-associated disease: antiviral therapy first [iv, b]. prognostic scores (hpll, malt-ipi) should be applied to estimate clinical behaviour [iii-iv, c]; btk and pi3k inhibitors may become options after short remissions [iii, b] not applicable clinical practice guideline 2020 trials across subtypes marginal zone lymphomas: gastric malt, non-gastric malt, nodal and splenic

d: Review of all patients with CLL/SLL seen at one center from 1975 to 2005: incidence, presentation, treatment outcome and prognostic factors of Richter syndrome, treated with chemotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy, with or without stem-cell transplantation

h: gcllsg pooled analysis (al-sawaf) frequency, characteristics and outcome of richter transformation among patients with advanced cll enrolled in first-line trials of the german cll study group 103 of 2,975 patients (3%) developed richter transformation: 95 diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (92%) and 8 hodgkin lymphoma (8%). median os from cll diagnosis 71 months with transformation vs 167 months without (hr 2.64, 95% ci 2.09–3.33). median os after transformation 9 months. 47 patients (46%) received chop-like regimens; 3 had an allogeneic and 2 an autologous transplant incidence of transformation; overall survival pooled analysis of trials 2021 risk, biology & diagnosis richter transformation

h: cibmtr transplant registry (herrera) autologous or allogeneic transplantation for richter syndrome of diffuse large b-cell type in the era of targeted therapy for cll after autologous transplant (53 patients, 66% in complete response): 3-year relapse 37%, pfs 48%, os 57%. after allogeneic transplant (118 patients, 34% in complete response, 33% with del(17p), 39% previously treated with novel agents): 3-year relapse 30%, pfs 43%, os 52%. after allogeneic transplant, depth of response determined outcome: 3-year pfs and os 66% and 77% in complete response, 43% and 57% in partial response, 5% and 15% with resistant disease. cytogenetic abnormalities and prior novel therapy did not affect outcome relapse, pfs and os at 3 years registry study 2021 chemoimmunotherapy & transplantation richter transformation

h: ace-cl-001, richter cohort (eyre) acalabrutinib 200 mg twice daily until progression in treatment-naive or previously treated richter transformation orr 40.0% (95% ci 21.1–61.3): complete response in 2 patients (8%) and partial response in 8 (32%). median duration of response 6.2 months (95% ci 0.3–14.8); median pfs 3.2 months (95% ci 1.8–4.0). median time on study 2.6 months safety and pharmacokinetics; response, duration of response and pfs were secondary phase 1/2 2021 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

d: Whole-genome, epigenome and transcriptome analysis with single-cell DNA and RNA sequencing of CLL developing Richter transformation, in longitudinal samples covering up to 19 years
h: early seeding of transformation (nadeu) whole-genome, epigenome and transcriptome analysis with single-cell dna and rna sequencing of cll developing richter transformation, in longitudinal samples covering up to 19 years minute subclones carrying the genomic, immunogenetic and transcriptomic features of richter cells were already present at cll diagnosis and remained dormant for up to 19 years before transformation. new driver alterations and a new mutational signature (sbs-rt) were identified. richter cells showed high oxidative phosphorylation and low b-cell receptor signaling, and inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation reduced their proliferation origin and drivers of the transformed clone genomic study 2022 risk, biology & diagnosis richter transformation

d: One cycle of dose-adjusted R-EPOCH, then an accelerated daily venetoclax ramp-up to 400 mg, then venetoclax with R-EPOCH for up to 5 more cycles; responders went on to venetoclax maintenance or cellular therapy

d: Blinatumomab by continuous infusion, escalated weekly to a maximum of 112 mcg per day, as an 8-week induction and a 4-week consolidation; patients had a median of 2 prior therapies for Richter syndrome, and all had a complex karyotype

d: Nivolumab every 2 weeks for up to 24 cycles with ibrutinib from cycle 2 until progression, in Richter transformation of diffuse large B-cell type; 42% had prior treatment for Richter transformation and 54% a prior BTK inhibitor
h: nivolumab-ibrutinib, md anderson phase 2 (jain) nivolumab every 2 weeks for up to 24 cycles with ibrutinib from cycle 2 until progression, in richter transformation of diffuse large b-cell type; 42% had prior treatment for richter transformation and 54% a prior btk inhibitor response in 10 of 24 patients (42%), with a median duration of response of 15 months. median os 13 months response phase 2 2023 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

h: zanubrutinib, alone or with tislelizumab (tam) zanubrutinib 160 mg twice daily until progression in richter transformation (13 patients), and zanubrutinib with tislelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks in relapsed richter transformation (7 patients), from two early-phase studies zanubrutinib alone: response in 8 of 13 patients (61.5%), complete in 2; estimated median duration of response 25.4 months and median pfs 17.3 months, at a median follow-up of 27.4 months. with tislelizumab: 7 patients, median follow-up 15.4 months; 5 progressed before 6 months and one was event-free at 51 months or more (all full paper) safety and response phase 1/2 (two studies) 2023 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

d: Tislelizumab with zanubrutinib for 12 cycles, followed by maintenance with both drugs in responders; 20.8% had received prior therapy for Richter transformation
h: rt1 (al-sawaf) tislelizumab with zanubrutinib for 12 cycles, followed by maintenance with both drugs in responders; 20.8% had received prior therapy for richter transformation orr 58.3% (95% ci 43.2–72.4), meeting the primary end point (p = 0.008): complete response 18.8%, partial response 39.6%. median duration of response not reached; median pfs 10.0 months (95% ci 3.8–16.3); 12-month os 74.7% (95% ci 58.4–91.0) overall response after six cycles, against a null hypothesis of 40% phase 2 2024 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

d: Obinutuzumab for 8 cycles, atezolizumab for 18 cycles and continuous venetoclax (CLL ramp-up, then 400 mg daily) for 35 cycles of 21 days, in previously untreated Richter transformation of diffuse large B-cell type

d: Venetoclax-based treatment of Richter transformation outside clinical trials: with a BTK inhibitor (28 patients), with R-CHOP (13) or with intensive chemoimmunotherapy other than R-CHOP (21)
h: venetoclax-based treatment, multicenter series (hampel) venetoclax-based treatment of richter transformation outside clinical trials: with a btk inhibitor (28 patients), with r-chop (13) or with intensive chemoimmunotherapy other than r-chop (21) best overall and complete response rates: 36% and 25% with a btk inhibitor, 54% and 46% with r-chop, 52% and 38% with intensive chemoimmunotherapy. median pfs and os: 4.9 and 14.3 months, 14.9 months and not reached, 3.3 and 9 months. del(17p) was associated with a lower complete response rate (odds ratio 0.15). prior venetoclax for cll was not significantly associated with outcome response, pfs and os retrospective series 2024 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

d: Pirtobrutinib 200 mg once daily in Richter transformation; 90% had received prior therapy directed at Richter transformation and 74% a covalent BTK inhibitor
h: bruin, richter cohort (wierda) pirtobrutinib 200 mg once daily in richter transformation; 90% had received prior therapy directed at richter transformation and 74% a covalent btk inhibitor orr 50.0% (95% ci 38.7–61.3): complete response in 11 patients (13%) and partial response in 30 (37%). orr 48.6% in the 74 patients with prior therapy for richter transformation and 62.5% in the 8 without. eight patients with ongoing response stopped pirtobrutinib to proceed to stem-cell transplantation. median duration of response 7.4 months (95% ci 3.1–19.1), with 45.9% of responses lasting 12 months; median pfs 3.7 months (95% ci 2.7–4.9); median os 12.5 months (95% ci 6.9–20.5), with 18-month os 44.3% (full paper) overall response phase 1/2 2024 btk, bcl2 & checkpoint inhibitors richter transformation

h: eric consensus recommendations (kittai) international expert consensus, coordinated by the european research initiative on cll, on the diagnosis, evaluation and research of richter transformation suspect transformation with rapid clinical decline, worsening b symptoms, elevated ldh or rapidly enlarging nodes. work-up should include pet-ct, and an excisional biopsy of an accessible lesion, preferably the most fdg-avid. the molecular relationship to the original cll clone should be defined. because no effective standard treatment exists, patients should be treated in a clinical trial. response of both the lymphoma and the cll should be assessed early, and trials should prioritize survival end points not applicable (recommendations) consensus statement 2025 risk, biology & diagnosis richter transformation

d: Multicenter series of Richter transformation of diffuse large B-cell type in patients who never received chemoimmunotherapy for CLL, in three groups: diagnosed together with CLL, CLL never treated, or CLL treated without chemoimmunotherapy (mostly targeted agents)
h: transformation without prior chemoimmunotherapy (kittai) multicenter series of richter transformation of diffuse large b-cell type in patients who never received chemoimmunotherapy for cll, in three groups: diagnosed together with cll, cll never treated, or cll treated without chemoimmunotherapy (mostly targeted agents) 79 patients diagnosed together with cll, 99 with untreated cll and 131 with prior non-chemoimmunotherapy treatment (58.0% a btk inhibitor only, 4.6% a bcl2 inhibitor only, 26.0% both). median os 25.8 months overall: 12.3 months after prior cll treatment vs 46.3 months (concurrent diagnosis) and 59.6 months (untreated cll). response to first-line treatment 57.8%, 84.0% and 70.8%. no first-line regimen was associated with better survival. median os 54.5 months after allogeneic transplant (46 patients) and 9.0 months after car t cells (55 patients). independent factors for shorter os: prior cll treatment (hr 2.08), older age, complex karyotype and higher ldh (all full paper) overall survival from transformation and factors predicting it retrospective series 2025 risk, biology & diagnosis richter transformation

d: European Hematology Association clinical practice guidelines on CLL, which for the first time include Richter transformation, replacing the earlier ESMO guidelines

d: Two cycles of bortezomib-dexamethasone followed by high-dose melphalan and stem cell transplantation vs transplantation alone, in newly diagnosed patients, all with renal involvement

d: Interphase FISH in 101 consecutive patients treated first-line with bortezomib-dexamethasone, ineligible for high-dose therapy, at Heidelberg; validated in 32 patients treated with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone
h: t(11;14) and bortezomib (bochtler) interphase fish in 101 consecutive patients treated first-line with bortezomib-dexamethasone, ineligible for high-dose therapy, at heidelberg; validated in 32 patients treated with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone with vs without t(11;14): median hematologic event-free survival 3.4 vs 8.8 months, os 8.7 vs 40.7 months, very good partial response or better 23% vs 47%. t(11;14) was independently adverse for hematologic event-free survival (hr 2.94) and os (hr 3.13). the myeloma high-risk abnormalities (t(4;14), t(14;16), del(17p), gain 1q21) were not adverse with bortezomib hematologic event-free survival, os and response by fish abnormality cohort study (cytogenetics) 2015 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Frontline cyclophosphamide, bortezomib and dexamethasone in 230 patients from European centres
h: cybord, european study (palladini) frontline cyclophosphamide, bortezomib and dexamethasone in 230 patients from european centres hematologic response 60% (62% in 201 patients with measurable disease), very good partial response or better 43%; cardiac response 17%, renal response 25%. stage iii with nt-probnp >8500 ng/l: response 42%, very good partial response or better 23%, median survival 7 months, but 2-year survival 67% in responders hematologic and organ response, survival cohort study (multicentre) 2015 newly diagnosed: plasma cell-directed therapy & transplantation al amyloidosis

d: 1,536 patients with AL amyloidosis transplanted at 134 North American centres (1995–2012), in three periods
h: cibmtr transplantation trends (d'souza) 1,536 patients with al amyloidosis transplanted at 134 north american centres (1995–2012), in three periods mortality at 30 and 100 days fell from 11% and 20% (1995–2000) to 5% and 11% (2001–2006) and 3% and 5% (2007–2012); 5-year os 55%, 61% and 77%. centres performing more than four al transplants a year had better survival; cardiac involvement predicted early mortality early mortality and overall survival registry study 2015 newly diagnosed: plasma cell-directed therapy & transplantation al amyloidosis

d: Bone scintigraphy and monoclonal protein tests in 1217 patients referred to specialist centres with suspected cardiac amyloidosis: 857 with histologically proven amyloid (374 by endomyocardial biopsy) and 360 with non-amyloid cardiomyopathy
h: nonbiopsy diagnosis of cardiac attr (gillmore) bone scintigraphy and monoclonal protein tests in 1217 patients referred to specialist centres with suspected cardiac amyloidosis: 857 with histologically proven amyloid (374 by endomyocardial biopsy) and 360 with non-amyloid cardiomyopathy myocardial uptake was more than 99% sensitive and 86% specific for cardiac attr amyloid; false positives came almost entirely from cardiac al amyloidosis. grade 2 or 3 uptake together with no monoclonal protein in serum or urine had a specificity and positive predictive value of 100% (95% ci of the positive predictive value 98.0–100) sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value for cardiac attr amyloid diagnostic study (multicentre) 2016 diagnosis & amyloid typing al amyloidosis

d: Monthly intravenous NEOD001, an antibody against misfolded light chain aggregates, at 0.5–24 mg/kg (3+3 design) in patients with persistent organ dysfunction after at least a partial hematologic response
h: neod001 (birtamimab) phase 1/2 (gertz) monthly intravenous neod001, an antibody against misfolded light chain aggregates, at 0.5–24 mg/kg (3+3 design) in patients with persistent organ dysfunction after at least a partial hematologic response no drug-related serious adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities or antidrug antibodies; recommended dose 24 mg/kg every 28 days. cardiac response in 8 of 14 evaluable patients (57%) and renal response in 9 of 15 (60%) maximum tolerated and recommended dose; safety phase 1/2 2016 fibril-directed therapy al amyloidosis

d: Prevalence of a monoclonal gammopathy (abnormal free light chain ratio or positive serum immunofixation) in patients with biopsy-proven wild-type ATTR or genopositive ATTR V122I amyloidosis at the Boston University Amyloidosis Center (2003–2016)
h: mgus in attr amyloidosis (phull) prevalence of a monoclonal gammopathy (abnormal free light chain ratio or positive serum immunofixation) in patients with biopsy-proven wild-type attr or genopositive attr v122i amyloidosis at the boston university amyloidosis center (2003–2016) a monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance was present in 55 of 140 patients with wild-type attr (39%) and 28 of 57 with attr v122i (49%) prevalence of mgus cohort study (retrospective) 2018 diagnosis & amyloid typing al amyloidosis

d: Derivation in 249 consecutive patients with BNP, NT-proBNP and troponin I measured together; survival tested in a complementary cohort of 592 patients with 10 years of follow-up
h: boston university bnp staging (lilleness) derivation in 249 consecutive patients with bnp, nt-probnp and troponin i measured together; survival tested in a complementary cohort of 592 patients with 10 years of follow-up bnp >81 pg/ml best matched mayo 2004 stage and identified cardiac involvement. stages by bnp >81 pg/ml and troponin i >0.1 ng/ml agreed with mayo 2004 (κ 0.854). in the survival cohort, stages i, ii, iii and iiib (25%, 44%, 15%, 16%) had median survival not reached, 9.4, 4.3 and 1 year overall survival prognostic model 2019 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Mass spectrometry-based proteomic typing of 16,175 amyloid specimens at one reference laboratory over 11 years (2008–2018)
h: mass spectrometry typing, 16,175 samples (dasari) mass spectrometry-based proteomic typing of 16,175 amyloid specimens at one reference laboratory over 11 years (2008–2018) 21 established types: al 59.0%, attr 28.4%, alect2 3.2%, aa 2.9%, heavy chain (ah) 2.3%, insulin 1.2%, and 15 rarer types below 1% each; organ-by-type and type-by-organ maps; amino acid substitutions of hereditary amyloidosis detected with 100% specificity frequency of amyloid types by organ laboratory series 2020 diagnosis & amyloid typing al amyloidosis

d: Open-label, multicentre randomized trial of melphalan-dexamethasone with or without bortezomib, stratified by cardiac stage; stage IIIb excluded
h: bmdex vs mdex (kastritis) open-label, multicentre randomized trial of melphalan-dexamethasone with or without bortezomib, stratified by cardiac stage; stage iiib excluded hematologic response at 3 months 79% vs 52% (p=0.002); very good partial or complete response 64% vs 39%; overall survival improved, with mortality halved (hr 0.50). grade 3–4 adverse events in 20% vs 10% of cycles hematologic response at 3 months phase 3 2020 newly diagnosed: plasma cell-directed therapy & transplantation al amyloidosis

d: Six 28-day cycles of intravenous daratumumab in 40 previously treated patients with dFLC >50 mg/L, at 15 centres
h: daratumumab monotherapy, relapsed (roussel) six 28-day cycles of intravenous daratumumab in 40 previously treated patients with dflc >50 mg/l, at 15 centres hematologic response in 22 patients; very good partial response or better 47.5%; median time to response 1 week; patients with no response after 4 doses rarely responded later. renal responses in 8 and cardiac in 7 patients. 2-year os 74% hematologic response phase 2 2020 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

d: Intravenous daratumumab 16 mg/kg (weekly for 8 weeks, every 2 weeks to week 24, then every 4 weeks) for up to 24 months in 22 previously treated patients
h: daratumumab monotherapy, relapsed (sanchorawala) intravenous daratumumab 16 mg/kg (weekly for 8 weeks, every 2 weeks to week 24, then every 4 weeks) for up to 24 months in 22 previously treated patients complete or very good partial response 86%; median time to first and best response 4 weeks and 3 months. renal response in 10 of 15 patients (67%), cardiac response in 7 of 14 (50%). no grade 3–4 infusion reactions safety, tolerability and hematologic response phase 2 2020 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

d: Bendamustine 100 mg/m² on days 1 and 2 with weekly dexamethasone 40 mg in 28-day cycles, after at least one previous therapy
h: bendamustine-dexamethasone (lentzsch) bendamustine 100 mg/m² on days 1 and 2 with weekly dexamethasone 40 mg in 28-day cycles, after at least one previous therapy partial response or better 57% (complete 11%, very good partial 18%); organ response 29% of 24 evaluable patients. median os 18.2 months, pfs 11.3 months. therapy-related grade 3–4 adverse events 65% partial hematologic response or better phase 2 2020 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

n: ESC position statement on cardiac amyloidosis (Garcia-Pavia)
d: Position statement of the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases
h: esc position statement on cardiac amyloidosis (garcia-pavia) position statement of the european society of cardiology working group on myocardial and pericardial diseases invasive and noninvasive definitions of cardiac amyloidosis, clinical scenarios that should raise suspicion, and a diagnostic algorithm that starts with scintigraphy together with serum free light chains and serum and urine immunofixation, with tissue typing when a monoclonal protein is found; also monitoring and treatment not applicable position statement 2021 diagnosis & amyloid typing al amyloidosis

d: Minimal residual disease by next-generation flow cytometry in 92 patients in hematologic complete response
h: mrd by next-generation flow (palladini) minimal residual disease by next-generation flow cytometry in 92 patients in hematologic complete response mrd persisted in 54% of patients in complete response (median 0.03% abnormal plasma cells). undetectable mrd was associated with more renal (90% vs 62%) and cardiac responses (95% vs 75%); hematologic progression at 1 year 0% with undetectable mrd vs 25% with persistent mrd organ response and hematologic progression by mrd status cohort study 2021 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Six cycles of bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone (VCd) with or without subcutaneous daratumumab, followed by daratumumab every 4 weeks for up to 24 cycles, in newly diagnosed patients; stage IIIb excluded
h: andromeda (kastritis) six cycles of bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone (vcd) with or without subcutaneous daratumumab, followed by daratumumab every 4 weeks for up to 24 cycles, in newly diagnosed patients; stage iiib excluded hematologic complete response 53.3% vs 18.1% (relative risk 2.9); major organ deterioration or hematologic progression-free survival favoured daratumumab (hr 0.58); cardiac responses at 6 months 41.5% vs 22.2%, renal 53.0% vs 23.9%. final analysis (61.4 mo): complete response 59.5% vs 19.2%; mod-pfs hr 0.44 and os hr 0.62; cardiac and renal responses 2 to 3 times more frequent hematologic complete response phase 3 2021 newly diagnosed: plasma cell-directed therapy & transplantation al amyloidosis

d: Venetoclax-containing regimens in 43 previously treated patients at 14 centres in the US and Europe; 31 with t(11;14)
h: venetoclax, t(11;14) (premkumar) venetoclax-containing regimens in 43 previously treated patients at 14 centres in the us and europe; 31 with t(11;14) hematologic response 68%, very good partial or complete 63%. with vs without t(11;14): response 81% vs 40%, very good partial or complete 78% vs 30%; median pfs not reached vs 6.7 months (hr 0.14). organ response 38%; grade ≥3 adverse events 19% hematologic response and pfs cohort study (retrospective, multicentre) 2021 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

d: Ixazomib-dexamethasone vs physician's choice (dexamethasone with or without melphalan, cyclophosphamide, thalidomide or lenalidomide) after 1–2 previous lines; the first phase 3 trial in relapsed disease
h: tourmaline-al1 (dispenzieri) ixazomib-dexamethasone vs physician's choice (dexamethasone with or without melphalan, cyclophosphamide, thalidomide or lenalidomide) after 1–2 previous lines; the first phase 3 trial in relapsed disease best hematologic response 53% vs 51% (p=0.76); complete response 26% vs 18%. median time to vital organ deterioration or death 34.8 vs 26.1 months (hr 0.53). median treatment duration 11.7 vs 5.0 months hematologic response rate; 2-year vital organ deterioration or death (only the first tested at this analysis) phase 3 2022 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

d: Open-label randomized trial in Mayo 2004 stage II–III disease: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily with 9 cycles of CyBorD vs CyBorD alone
h: doxycycline with cybord (shen) open-label randomized trial in mayo 2004 stage ii–iii disease: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily with 9 cycles of cybord vs cybord alone progression in 45.7% vs 42.9%; pfs hr 0.97 (95% ci 0.59–1.60; p=0.91). no differences in cardiac pfs (hr 0.91) or os (hr 1.04); deaths 35.7% in each group 2-year progression-free survival (death, hematologic or organ progression) randomized trial (multicentre) 2022 fibril-directed therapy al amyloidosis

d: 651 patients with at least a hematologic partial response and evaluable cardiac involvement; four levels of response by depth of NT-proBNP or BNP fall, as best response and at 6, 12 and 24 months
h: graded cardiac response criteria (muchtar) 651 patients with at least a hematologic partial response and evaluable cardiac involvement; four levels of response by depth of nt-probnp or bnp fall, as best response and at 6, 12 and 24 months best cardiac complete response 16%, very good partial response 26.4%, partial response 22.9%, no response 34.7%. cardiac complete response more frequent in stage ii than iiia and iiib (22% vs 13.5% vs 3.2%). 5-year os 93%, 79%, 65% and 33% by level; four levels predicted survival better than two from 12 months overall survival response criteria (multicentre validation) 2023 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of birtamimab 24 mg/kg every 28 days with standard of care in newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients
h: vital, birtamimab (gertz) double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of birtamimab 24 mg/kg every 28 days with standard of care in newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients stopped early for futility: no difference in the primary end point (hr 0.826; p=0.303). post hoc, in mayo stage iv, time to all-cause mortality improved at 9 months (hr 0.413; 74% vs 49% alive). adverse event rates similar time to all-cause mortality or adjudicated cardiac hospitalization ≥91 days after the first infusion phase 3 2023 fibril-directed therapy al amyloidosis

d: Consecutive patients newly diagnosed with AL amyloidosis at the UK National Amyloidosis Centre (2015–2021) with echocardiography, biomarkers and cardiac MRI with extracellular volume (ECV) mapping at diagnosis
h: extracellular volume by cardiac mri (porcari) consecutive patients newly diagnosed with al amyloidosis at the uk national amyloidosis centre (2015–2021) with echocardiography, biomarkers and cardiac mri with extracellular volume (ecv) mapping at diagnosis ecv was independently associated with mortality over a median of 40.5 months. at 6 months, survival did not depend on hematologic response when ecv was <0.30, needed at least partial response with ecv 0.31–0.40, and needed complete response with ecv >0.40. with ecv >0.40, deep response at 1 month was associated with better survival than at 6 months all-cause mortality and the hematologic response needed by ecv group cohort study (prospective imaging) 2024 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Cooperative-group trial of isatuximab 20 mg/kg (weekly in cycle 1, then every 2 weeks through cycle 24) in relapsed AL amyloidosis
h: swog s1702, isatuximab (parker) cooperative-group trial of isatuximab 20 mg/kg (weekly in cycle 1, then every 2 weeks through cycle 24) in relapsed al amyloidosis among 35 evaluable patients, hematologic response 77.1%, very good partial response or better 57%; median time to partial response 1.1 months. renal response 7 of 14 (50%), cardiac response 8 of 14 (57%). treatment-related grade ≥3 lymphopenia 8.5%, infection 6% hematologic response phase 2 2025 relapsed disease al amyloidosis

d: AL International Staging System derived at the UK National Amyloidosis Centre (2015–2019) and validated in cohorts from Greece, Italy, the Netherlands, Switzerland, the US and the UK (2015–2024), adding echocardiographic longitudinal strain to NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity troponin T
h: al-iss with stage iiic (khwaja) al international staging system derived at the uk national amyloidosis centre (2015–2019) and validated in cohorts from greece, italy, the netherlands, switzerland, the us and the uk (2015–2024), adding echocardiographic longitudinal strain to nt-probnp and high-sensitivity troponin t longitudinal strain ≥−9%, nt-probnp (332 and 8500 ng/l) and high-sensitivity troponin t ≥50 ng/l were independent; stages i, ii, iiia, iiib and iiic. validation cohort (43% treated first-line with daratumumab): 17%, 41%, 29%, 9% and 5%; median os not reached for stages i–ii, 67, 26 and 7 months for iiia, iiib and iiic. among daratumumab-treated patients, 1-year os 53% in iiic vs 68% in iiib. harrell c 0.69 overall survival prognostic model (international validation) 2026 staging, prognosis & response criteria al amyloidosis

d: Prospective European Myeloma Network trial of daratumumab monotherapy for up to 2 years in previously untreated patients with Mayo 2004/European stage IIIB disease; bortezomib and dexamethasone could be added for inadequate response after 3 cycles
h: emn22, daratumumab in stage iiib (kastritis) prospective european myeloma network trial of daratumumab monotherapy for up to 2 years in previously untreated patients with mayo 2004/european stage iiib disease; bortezomib and dexamethasone could be added for inadequate response after 3 cycles 6-month os 65% (95% ci 48.2–77.6), median os 10.4 months; best hematologic response by 6 months 75% (very good partial response or better 47.5%, complete 12.5%); median time to first response 1 week. cardiac response at 6 months 30%. ten patients (25%) needed bortezomib-dexamethasone 6-month overall survival phase 2 2026 newly diagnosed: plasma cell-directed therapy & transplantation al amyloidosis

d: Two randomized, placebo-controlled trials in newly diagnosed patients with European modification of Mayo 2004 stage IIIa or IIIb disease: anselamimab, a fibril-binding antibody, or placebo with CyBorD (with or without daratumumab)
h: cares, anselamimab (wechalekar) two randomized, placebo-controlled trials in newly diagnosed patients with european modification of mayo 2004 stage iiia or iiib disease: anselamimab, a fibril-binding antibody, or placebo with cybord (with or without daratumumab) win ratio 1.11 (p=0.332); all-cause mortality hr 0.80 (p=0.290); cardiovascular hospitalizations 0.59 vs 0.89 per patient-year (p=0.145). in κ isotype (72 patients): win ratio 2.06 (p=0.100), mortality hr 0.38 and hospitalization rate ratio 0.29 (nominal p values), with better kansas city cardiomyopathy questionnaire scores; no benefit with λ isotype. safety similar between arms hierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations (win ratio) phase 3 (two trials) 2026 fibril-directed therapy al amyloidosis
